title: Clinical and orthoptic outcomes after trapdoor fracture repair in adult and pediatric population: a cohort study
html: Orbital trapdoor fractures, traditionally considered a pediatric injury, also occur in adults and may present with distinct clinical presentation and management. This cohort study compares adult and pediatric patients with orbital trapdoor fractures and evaluates clinical presentation, radiological findings, operative management, and long-term clinical and orthoptic outcomes, as well as the influence of surgical timing by comparing early (within 2 days) versus late (after 2 days) intervention. Nineteen patients (12 children and seven adults) with clinically and computed tomography-confirmed trapdoor fractures who were surgically treated at the Erasmus Medical Center between 2012 and 2024 and had at least 3 months of follow-up were analyzed retrospectively.
